Heard the learned counsel for petitioner and the learned High Court Government Pleader and perused the material on record.

2. Crime No.60/2023 of Jagajeevanram Nagar Police Station is registered against the petitioner for offence punishable under Section 341, 498A, 504 and 307 of IPC on a complaint lodged by his wife Smt.Shama.
3. This petition is filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. to enlarge the petitioner on bail.

4. The complaint averments reveal that the complainant's marriage with petitioner took place about 21 years prior to the date of incident and it was a love marriage but due to the harassment by the petitioner, she was residing separately at Vinayakanagar along with her NC: 2023:KHC:24928 son since 2-3 years.

It is alleged that the petitioner has taken second wife and he was residing with her and whenever he was visiting the house of the complainant he used to harass and abuse her and her daughter saying that they are leading immoral life etc.

It is further alleged that on 02.05.2023 at about 9.30 a.m., when the complainant was going by walk near 2nd cross, Vinayakanagar, all of a sudden, petitioner came and stopped the complainant and started abusing her in filthy language and took a bottle of petrol and poured on her and tried to set fire.
When the complainant started screaming, he ran away from the spot seeing the public approaching.
5. The complainant has not sustained any injuries.
The allegations are that the petitioner poured kerosene on the complainant and tried to set fire and thus made an attempt on her life.
The said allegations have to be established in due course.
Admittedly, the marriage between the petitioner and complainant has taken place NC: 2023:KHC:24928 about 21 years prior to the date of incident.
As per complaint averments, the petitioner has taken a second wife.
It appears that there is a matrimonial dispute between the petitioner and his wife and their relationship is not cordial.
6. Petitioner was arrested on 02.05.2023 and he is in judicial custody.
He is not required for custodial interrogation.
He has no criminal antecedents.
He has undertaken to abide by conditions.
Hence, by imposing necessary conditions, the relief sought by the petitioner can be granted.

Accordingly, the following:
ORDER i. Petition is allowed.
